insect_or_comparison: Bombus terrestris audax vs Apis mellifera mellifera and Andrena carantonica
toxin_or_defense: grayanotoxin I and III at nectar-realistic concentrations
phenotype_evidence: B. terrestris audax showed no mortality or behavioral effect, including parasite and food-stress tests; A. mellifera mellifera had strong GTX-I mortality; Andrena showed sublethal malaise and reduced feeding
causal_or_genetic_evidence: Controlled non-choice feeding assays; no published causal gene test
relevance_to_Apis_laboriosa: B. terrestris is the strongest available same-toxin evolutionary comparator
limit: A. laboriosa was not tested; Andrena is not a clean tolerant phenotype; oral assays do not identify mechanism; available genome references are not the assayed populations

phenotype_evidence: A. cerana had higher survival, learning, and memory tolerance than A. mellifera during matched short- and long-term feeding
causal_or_genetic_evidence: Controlled consumption, survival, and proboscis-extension learning assays; no causal gene test
relevance_to_Apis_laboriosa: Close pollinator precedent that sympatric exposure can track a species-level tolerance difference
limit: Different toxin; both species were affected at sufficient dose; coevolution is supported by geography and phenotype but the mechanism was not established

insect_or_comparison: 18 insects spanning 15 genera and four orders
causal_or_genetic_evidence: Repeated ATPalpha substitutions, including N122H previously shown to confer resistance
relevance_to_Apis_laboriosa: Positive control: when target-site resistance is recurrent, homologous functional-site changes can be visible across distant insects
limit: Different toxin and target; some adapted insects lack target-site substitutions and may use exclusion, excretion, or compartmentalization

phenotype_evidence: Larvae feed on defended Brassicales tissue without apparent toxic effect
causal_or_genetic_evidence: Gut nitrile-specifier protein redirects hydrolysis away from toxic isothiocyanates; resulting nitriles are excreted
relevance_to_Apis_laboriosa: Direct biochemical precedent for protecting internal tissues before toxin exposure
limit: Different toxin, life stage, and insect order; does not identify a bee ortholog

phenotype_evidence: Larvae tolerate and efficiently excrete ingested nicotine
causal_or_genetic_evidence: Plant-mediated RNAi of midgut-induced CYP6B46 changes nicotine transfer from gut to hemolymph and defensive exhalation; only about 0.65% is redirected
relevance_to_Apis_laboriosa: Shows that a single regulated gut enzyme can control systemic exposure without broad family expansion
limit: Different toxin and ecological function; CYP6B46 moves a small nicotine fraction into hemolymph rather than simply blocking uptake

phenotype_evidence: D. sechellia resists otherwise toxic Morinda fruit; resistance maps to multiple loci
causal_or_genetic_evidence: RNAi implicates Osi6, Osi7, and Osi8; Osi6 and Osi7 lack fixed derived amino-acid changes and show tissue-specific expression effects
mechanism_class: barrier or trafficking-family regulation and polygenic adaptation
relevance_to_Apis_laboriosa: Shows why protein sequence and gene counts can miss regulatory, tissue-specific toxin adaptation
limit: Different toxin and tissue biology; Osiris proteins remain incompletely characterized
